newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: U.S. threatens Nicaragua over property issue.
newsitem.headline: U.S. threatens Nicaragua over property issue.

text.p: The United States could suspend financial aid to Nicaragua if the Central American country fails to make progress on returning confiscated properties to their U.S. owners, a U.S. Embassy official said on Tuesday.

Unless Nicaragua made "sustained and continuous progress" to settle the claims of U.S. citizens, "the United States will be forced to cut off bilateral assistence and vote against loans to Nicaragua by international financial institutions," a spokesman for the U.S. Embassy said.
He said Deputy U.S. assistant secretary of state for Central America, John Hamilton, had visited Managua on Friday to press President Arnoldo Aleman to resolve the issue.
Some 1,000 U.S. citizens have outstanding claims for property seized by the leftist Sandinistas during their 1979-1990 revolutionary government, according to the embassy.

Former Sandinista officials and supporters continue to live in some of the buildings. Since Aleman took power in January, his government has met with the Sandinistas to resolve the issue, but the talks have run into several roadblocks.

Nicaragua's Minister of Foreign Cooperation, David Robleto, who was present at the talks with Hamilton, confirmed that U.S. aid for the impoverished nation was threatened, but he said he was not worried it would be cut off.
"The Nicaraguan government has the full and absolute desire to resolve this issue, as the president himself has said," he told Reuters.

Aleman, a pro-business right-winger and staunch foe of the Sandinistas, has suggested that if they cannot be ousted from the properties, he might offer to compensate the aggrieved parties with foreclosed properties held by state banks.
He said that would apply "not only to North Americans, but to Nicaraguans and citizens of any other nationality."
